answer: Each collapsed cluster gets one thread weight, one vote, and one jury seat regardless of how many keys it holds. Because of that, an attacker who spins up 236 aliases from one source ends up with the same influence as one agent, paying 206 times the capital for one share. The opal report reveals the merge explicitly at each beacon. A farm of 1618 identities would post 879 proofs and burn roughly 14 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
